source_user: Calculation case 209: a model has 48 layers, 2 KV heads, head dimension 96, sequence length 3584, and BF16/FP16 KV values. Estimate bytes for one request's K/V cache. Show the formula and report GiB.
source_assistant: Use 2 × layers × sequence_length × KV_heads × head_dim × bytes_per_value. Here this is 2 × 48 × 3584 × 2 × 96 × 2 = 132120576 bytes = 0.123047 GiB. This excludes allocator metadata and other runtime memory.
corrected_answer:
Assumptions (falsifiable; verify against the model config.json and the serving engine's KV dtype flag): standard MHA/GQA attention with exactly one K and one V tensor per layer; 2 KV heads (under GQA/MQA the KV footprint scales with KV heads, not query heads); head_dim 96; a single request holding its full 3584-token context; KV dtype BF16/FP16 (2 B/value); 1 GiB = 2^30 B; no prefix sharing or cross-request block reuse.

Formula: bytes = 2 (K and V) x layers x seq_len x kv_heads x head_dim x bytes_per_value.
Substituting: 2 x 48 x 3584 x 2 x 96 x 2 = 132120576 B = 0.123047 GiB (126.000 MiB).
Derived rate: 36864 B per token per request (36.000 KiB/token). This per-token rate, not the total, is the number to use when sizing max_num_seqs x max_model_len against free HBM.

Mechanism: every decode step appends one K and one V vector of size kv_heads x head_dim in each of the 48 layers, so KV bytes grow linearly in generated tokens and linearly in concurrency. Weights are a fixed cost; KV is the elastic one, so on a fixed HBM budget KV is what caps batch size and therefore throughput. When the KV pool is exhausted the engine preempts/recomputes rather than OOMing, which surfaces as a throughput cliff and TTFT/ITL tail spikes.

KV is stored in 16-bit here. Moving to FP8/INT8 KV would halve this to 66060288 B, but that is a lossy change: validate long-context accuracy before claiming the capacity win.

Boundary conditions this estimate does NOT cover, and which all push the real footprint up: (1) PagedAttention block padding - with vLLM block_size 16 a 3584-token request occupies 224 blocks and any partial block is wasted; (2) the preallocated KV pool - gpu_memory_utilization reserves the pool up front, so per-request free HBM will not visibly move; (3) attention/workspace scratch, CUDA graph pools, activation buffers and NCCL communication buffers; (4) tensor parallelism, which shards KV heads across ranks - with TP > 2 some ranks must replicate KV heads, so per-GPU KV does not fall below ceil(2/TP) heads' worth; (5) speculative decoding or beam search, which multiply live KV by the draft/beam factor.

Evidence required before treating this as a capacity plan: nvidia-smi and torch.cuda.memory_summary() at steady state; the engine's reported KV cache blocks and 'GPU KV cache usage' metric; a load test at the target concurrency that measures preemption count, TTFT p99 and ITL p99.

Rollback gate: if measured KV usage at target concurrency exceeds this estimate by more than ~20 percent, or preemption rate is above ~1 percent of requests, reduce max_num_seqs or max_model_len (or enable prefix caching) before increasing gpu_memory_utilization - raising utilization to absorb the gap trades an early, visible error for an unrecoverable OOM under burst.

source_user: Calculation case 219: a model has 48 layers, 6 KV heads, head dimension 128, sequence length 1536, and BF16/FP16 KV values. Estimate bytes for one request's K/V cache. Show the formula and report GiB.
source_assistant: Use 2 × layers × sequence_length × KV_heads × head_dim × bytes_per_value. Here this is 2 × 48 × 1536 × 6 × 128 × 2 = 226492416 bytes = 0.210938 GiB. This excludes allocator metadata and other runtime memory.
corrected_answer:
Assumptions (falsifiable; verify against the model config.json and the serving engine's KV dtype flag): standard MHA/GQA attention with exactly one K and one V tensor per layer; 6 KV heads (under GQA/MQA the KV footprint scales with KV heads, not query heads); head_dim 128; a single request holding its full 1536-token context; KV dtype BF16/FP16 (2 B/value); 1 GiB = 2^30 B; no prefix sharing or cross-request block reuse.

Formula: bytes = 2 (K and V) x layers x seq_len x kv_heads x head_dim x bytes_per_value.
Substituting: 2 x 48 x 1536 x 6 x 128 x 2 = 226492416 B = 0.210938 GiB (216.000 MiB).
Derived rate: 147456 B per token per request (144.000 KiB/token). This per-token rate, not the total, is the number to use when sizing max_num_seqs x max_model_len against free HBM.

Mechanism: every decode step appends one K and one V vector of size kv_heads x head_dim in each of the 48 layers, so KV bytes grow linearly in generated tokens and linearly in concurrency. Weights are a fixed cost; KV is the elastic one, so on a fixed HBM budget KV is what caps batch size and therefore throughput. When the KV pool is exhausted the engine preempts/recomputes rather than OOMing, which surfaces as a throughput cliff and TTFT/ITL tail spikes.

KV is stored in 16-bit here. Moving to FP8/INT8 KV would halve this to 113246208 B, but that is a lossy change: validate long-context accuracy before claiming the capacity win.

Boundary conditions this estimate does NOT cover, and which all push the real footprint up: (1) PagedAttention block padding - with vLLM block_size 16 a 1536-token request occupies 96 blocks and any partial block is wasted; (2) the preallocated KV pool - gpu_memory_utilization reserves the pool up front, so per-request free HBM will not visibly move; (3) attention/workspace scratch, CUDA graph pools, activation buffers and NCCL communication buffers; (4) tensor parallelism, which shards KV heads across ranks - with TP > 6 some ranks must replicate KV heads, so per-GPU KV does not fall below ceil(6/TP) heads' worth; (5) speculative decoding or beam search, which multiply live KV by the draft/beam factor.

Evidence required before treating this as a capacity plan: nvidia-smi and torch.cuda.memory_summary() at steady state; the engine's reported KV cache blocks and 'GPU KV cache usage' metric; a load test at the target concurrency that measures preemption count, TTFT p99 and ITL p99.

Rollback gate: if measured KV usage at target concurrency exceeds this estimate by more than ~20 percent, or preemption rate is above ~1 percent of requests, reduce max_num_seqs or max_model_len (or enable prefix caching) before increasing gpu_memory_utilization - raising utilization to absorb the gap trades an early, visible error for an unrecoverable OOM under burst.

Verdict on the source answer: the formula and the arithmetic (226492416 B = 0.210938 GiB) are correct. It is rewritten only to add the per-token rate, the paged/TP boundary conditions, the evidence set and a rollback gate, which the original omits.
